question: Is foreign money really fleeing India? What FDI and FII numbers actually mean.

theme.label: Economy and public money
readerQuestions: What is the headline economic number?
Is this a total number or a per-person number?
How much of the story is prices, exchange rates, or GDP share?
What does this explain about household life?

plannedCharts.title: The number everyone is panicking about
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Net FDI fell from about $43bn (FY20) to under $1bn (FY25). Every headline screams this.

plannedCharts.title: Patient money and hot money
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The two kinds of foreign money behave completely differently.

plannedCharts.title: Gross inflows hit a record the year net 'collapsed'
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Foreigners did not stop coming. Gross inflows actually rose to a record ~$81bn.

plannedCharts.title: What eats the gap: repatriation and Indians investing abroad
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Net = gross minus repatriation minus outward FDI. Both subtractions grew.

plannedCharts.title: Foreign investors are taking profits home
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Repatriation and disinvestment are why a flow turns negative, and they are rising.

plannedCharts.title: India has quietly become a capital exporter
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Indian firms now hold a large and growing stock of investments abroad.

plannedCharts.title: And the yearly outflow has doubled
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The annual pace of Indian investment abroad roughly doubled in five years.

plannedCharts.title: Hot money, month by month
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Portfolio flows are violent at monthly resolution, which is the point of 'hot money'.

plannedCharts.title: Three wild years in a row
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Even annually, FII swings between large inflows and outflows.

plannedCharts.title: Equity walked out while debt poured in
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Lumping 'FII' together hides that equity and debt often move in opposite directions.

plannedCharts.title: The bond-index moment
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A structural event, not sentiment, drove the recent debt inflows.

plannedCharts.title: The real trigger sits in Washington
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: When the dollar strengthens against emerging-market currencies, money leaves India.

plannedCharts.title: The US rate cycle pulls the strings
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Higher US rates make safe US assets more attractive than emerging-market risk.

plannedCharts.title: When the world gets scared, India gets sold
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: FII is risk-on/risk-off money; spikes in global fear coincide with outflows.

plannedCharts.title: What actually moves FII money
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Putting the global drivers side by side: all of them pull the same way.

plannedCharts.title: FDI 'comes from' tiny tax-treaty hubs
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Two small jurisdictions account for nearly half of India's cumulative FDI.

plannedCharts.title: But portfolio money is real American money
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Flip to portfolio holdings and the tax-haven pattern vanishes.

plannedCharts.title: And it goes into services, not factories
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Where the money lands is as revealing as where it comes from.

plannedCharts.title: India is a small slice of world FDI
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Zoom out and India's recent dip is partly a global FDI slowdown, not just India's.

plannedCharts.title: Still well behind the leaders
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Against peers, India attracts less FDI than its size might suggest.
